svg.text: T34 • LETHAL TRIFECTA VENN
BEST FOR: 5-SECOND AGENT SECURITY TEST
GOOGLE CLOUD + OPEN-SOURCE PARITY
FORMAT LINEAGE: Simon Willison, The lethal trifecta for AI agents (Jun 2025)
The Lethal Trifecta: If Your Agent Has All Three, Someone Can Make It Leak
Simon Willison's five-second security test. Private data + untrusted content + a way to send things out = exfiltration waiting for the right PDF.
ACCESS TO PRIVATE DATA
inbox, CRM, database, source code,
files
EXPOSURE TO UNTRUSTED CONTENT
web pages, PDFs, emails, tickets,
tool results
ABILITY TO COMMUNICATE OUT
send email, POST webhook, open URL, write issue
LETHAL
TRIFECTA
data walks out
Dots are placed by which legs each setup has; the red core is the only region where a prompt injection becomes a data breach.
SIX REAL SETUPS — WHICH LEGS DO THEY HAVE?
Inbox assistant that reads and sends mail
ALL THREE
A crafted email can instruct it to forward your threads.
Browser agent using your logged-in sessions
ALL THREE
Any page it visits can steer it; it can act as you.
Coding agent in a sandbox with no network
DATA + UNTRUSTED
Repo + issues are untrusted, but nothing can leave the box.
Public web researcher, no private data
UNTRUSTED + OUT
Can be hijacked, but has nothing of yours to leak.
Internal SQL analyst, no web, no sending
DATA ONLY
Reads sensitive data; no untrusted input, no exit.
Doc summarizer with write tools unmounted
DATA + UNTRUSTED
Capability downgrade removed the third leg at runtime.
THE FIX IS STRUCTURAL: REMOVE ONE LEG
Remove 'communicate out' while reading untrusted content
Taint the session on ingress; unmount send_email / webhook / URL tools (ADK
taint guard, LangGraph state flag, OPA policy).
Remove 'private data' from the reading agent
Split roles: one agent reads the web with no data access, another with data
access never sees raw web content.
Make 'communicate out' require a human
Any outbound action after untrusted input needs a signed approval (Cloud IAP
JWT, Keycloak) — the model cannot forge it.
Scanners (Model Armor, Llama Guard) lower the odds; removing a leg removes the outcome.
Curated by Nitin Aggarwal • Google Cloud ADK + OpenHands Factory • Proprietary + Confidential
